title: Crunching Numbers
briefing: Head office wants numbers before they'll fund the production lines. How many parts can we make, what will it cost, and are we over budget? The calculator terminal gives you the day's figures. They change every day, so your code has to work them out, not just remember today's answers.
hints: You already have parts_per_hour, hours, cost_per_part, budget and is_powered. Multiply with *, and use // for whole boxes and % for the leftovers.
over_budget is a comparison: total_cost > budget gives True or False. can_run uses the logical operators and and not.

total_parts = parts_per_hour * hours, total_cost = total_parts * cost_per_part, boxes = total_parts // 12, leftover = total_parts % 12, over_budget = total_cost > budget, can_run = is_powered and not over_budget
bonus: Work out what percentage of the budget you'd spend: total_cost / budget * 100. Then round it with round(value, 1).
